correctness.rationale: The exact down-set argument bounds every cube point by its all-ones distance; the coordinatewise strictness gives all-point uniqueness for both families. Cauchy–Schwarz plus a maximum-independent-set mixture yields the sharp graph-wide equality characterization. Path hull integrality follows from bipartite total unimodularity. Explicit rational nonnegative edge multipliers satisfy all KKT identities, and the completed-square identity proves global optimality for each integer n, including n=2 and odd n=3. Cycles are vertex transitive with exact independence number floor(n/2). The odd-order squared-distance difference is direct subtraction. The actual packaged verification script passes exact rational and independent numerical checks, but finite code is not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: This answers a natural geometric question for all two basic connected bounded-degree graph families: the complete Euclidean loss when the Boolean cube is constrained to integral independent-set vectors, with unique deepest points and explicit nearest coordinates. The exact parity-dependent single-edge perturbation (zero versus a positive asymptotically constant squared metric defect) is a structural stability distinction, not merely a small finite or tabulated example. A general graph tightness characterization ties the metric sharply to uniform maximum-independent-set marginals and diagnoses the odd-path difference.
